items.body:
# Bug Backlog Analysis: Moment.js Issue Tracker Health (September 2026)

## Overview

This issue presents a quantitative analysis of the Moment.js issue tracker, examining the gap between incoming bug reports and resolution velocity. The data reveals a significant and growing backlog — one that the "maintenance mode" status alone does not fully account for.

---

## Key Metrics

### Aging Open Issues
| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Open issues created **before 2023** | **46** |
| Open issues created **before 2020** | **~25** |
| Oldest open bug (still relevant) | [#2928](https://github.com/moment/moment/issues/2928) — Jan 2016 (10+ years) |
| Bugs labeled "Bug" still open | **5** |
| Bugs with other issue-type labels (DST, Duration, etc.) still open | **~45** |
| Open issues from 2025+ | **3** |

### Resolution Rate (2025–2026)
| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Total issues closed in 2025–2026 | **36** |
| Actual bug fixes among those closures | **~1** (#6295, closed July 2026) |
| Spam / invalid / non-bug closures | **~30** (e.g., #6334, #6332, #6340, #6342 — spam, bounty pitches, off-topic) |
| Genuine bug reports closed as completed | **~1** |
| **Effective bug resolution rate** | **~1 bug fixed in ~20 months** |

### The "Known Issue" Label Pattern
Multiple significant bugs have been labeled `Known Issue` — a label whose description references issue #6373 (now deleted/private) — effectively acknowledging them without any plan for resolution:

- [#5515](https://github.com/moment/moment/issues/5515): Different `utcOffset()` results in Firefox vs Chrome — "Known Issue"
- Several other DST and fractional-offset issues are similarly labeled

---

## Specific Long-Standing Bugs (with Details)

### 1. [#2928](https://github.com/moment/moment/issues/2928) — Duration days inconsistent (Bug, Duration bubble issues)
- **Opened:** January 28, **2016** (over 10 years)
- **Author:** @juhamust
- **Summary:** `moment.duration(0.123, 'years').days()` returns `0`, but `moment.duration(0.123 * 365, 'days').days()` returns `~13.89`
- **Comments:** 6 | **Reactions:** 0
- **Status:** Still open, last update May 2020

### 2. [#3706](https://github.com/moment/moment/issues/3706) — `.startOf("hour")` wrong across DST boundaries (Bug, DST)
- **Opened:** January 6, **2017** (over 9 years)
- **Author:** @colinhunt
- **Summary:** `moment.tz("2017-04-02T01:30:00+10:30", "Australia/Lord_Howe").startOf("hour")` returns `01:30+11:00` instead of `01:00+11:00`
- **Comments:** 1 | **Reactions:** 0
- **Status:** Still open, updated Aug 2026

### 3. [#3980](https://github.com/moment/moment/issues/3980) — Incorrect month diff when time involved (Bug)
- **Opened:** May 26, **2017** (over 9 years)
- **Author:** @standy
- **Summary:** `b.diff(a, 'M')` where b > c produces transitivity violation: `c - a` should be ≥ `b - a` but is 0 vs 1
- **Comments:** 5 | **Reactions:** 0
- **Status:** Still open, updated Sept 2026

### 4. [#4127](https://github.com/moment/moment/issues/4127) — from()/to() wrong days calculation around month boundary (Bug)
- **Opened:** August 17, **2017** (over 9 years)
- **Author:** @pretender
- **Summary:** `now.to(expiredAt)` and `tomorrow.to(expiredAt)` both return `'30 days ago'` despite being a full day apart
- **Comments:** 5 | **Reactions:** 👍 2
- **Status:** Still open, updated Sept 2026

### 5. [#5515](https://github.com/moment/moment/issues/5515) — Different `utcOffset()` in Firefox vs Chrome (Known Issue)
- **Opened:** May 6, **2020** (over 6 years)
- **Author:** @heroboy
- **Summary:** Historical dates produce different UTC offsets across browsers (486 min in Chrome, -485.7 min in Firefox for the same date)
- **Comments:** 6 | **Reactions:** 👍 1
- **Status:** Still open, labeled "Known Issue", updated Sept 2026

### 6. [#6440](https://github.com/moment/moment/issues/6440) — `moment.locale('__proto__')` corrupts global locale
- **Opened:** September 4, **2026** (new but critical)
- **Author:** @UlisesGascon
- **Summary:** Passing `'__proto__'` to `moment.locale()` corrupts the global locale object and breaks formatting
- **Comments:** 0 | **Reactions:** 0
- **Status:** Fresh, no response yet

---

## Patterns Observed

### 1. Single-Point-of-Failure Maintainer Model
The commit history shows that essentially all recent commits (Aug–Sept 2026) are from a single contributor (@mattjohnsonpint). While their work is high-quality and appreciated, this creates a bottleneck where one person's bandwidth determines the entire project's velocity.

### 2. "Maintenance Mode" as a De-Facto Freeze
The README declares "maintenance mode" and states "new features are not being accepted." However, in practice, even bug fixes are barely trickling through (1 bug fixed in ~20 months). The project is effectively in **life-support mode**, not maintenance mode.

### 3. Triage Without Resolution
Many issues have been triaged with labels like `Known Issue`, `Duration bubble issues`, `relative time threshold issues`, `Fractional-Hour UTC Offset` — these are effectively graveyards. They acknowledge the bug without any timeline, milestone, or assignee for resolution.

### 4. Disproportionate Spam Consumption
Of the 36 issues closed in 2025–2026, approximately 30 (~83%) were spam, off-topic, or invalid posts. This means the limited maintainer attention is disproportionately consumed by issue triage rather than actual fixes.

### 5. Massive User Base, Minimal Support
Moment.js still has:
- **~48,000 GitHub stars**
- **~12 million weekly npm downloads**
- Used in **~4 million+ dependent repositories**

This is an enormous user base relying on a library with effectively frozen bug resolution.

### 6. No Clear Migration Path Enforced
While the README recommends alternatives (Luxon, Day.js, date-fns, js-joda), there is no deprecation timeline, no runtime warnings encouraging migration, and no plan to actively guide the massive user base away.

---

## Recommendations

1. **Add deprecation warnings at runtime** — a non-breaking console.warn on `moment()` import that points users to alternatives
2. **Close or explicitly acknowledge all pre-2020 bugs** — if they won't be fixed, say so clearly and close them to reduce noise
3. **Invite more maintainers** — specifically for triage to filter spam and reduce the bottleneck on @mattjohnsonpint
4. **Create a migration guide** as a pinned issue — practical recipes for common Moment.js patterns in Luxon / Day.js / date-fns
5. **Consider archiving the repo** — if the project is truly in life-support mode, archiving with a clear sunset notice would be more honest to the community than the current state

---

*This analysis was compiled by examining the issue tracker on September 9, 2026, using GitHub's API. Data is publicly available and verifiable.*
items.title: [Analysis] Issue Backlog Health Check: 46+ bugs open from pre-2023, 1 bug fixed in ~20 months — the "maintenance mode" gap

items.body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I searched existing issues for this problem.
- [x] I read the applicable documentation and guides.
- [x] I reproduced the problem with the latest Moment.js release.
- [x] I confirmed this belongs to Moment.js core, not Moment Timezone, Luxon, or the momentjs.com website.

### Description

The internal locale registry is a plain object (`var locales = {}`), and `loadLocale(name)` decides a locale is already loaded with `if (locales[name] !== undefined)`. For the name `__proto__`, `locales['__proto__']` returns `Object.prototype` through the built-in `__proto__` accessor, which is not `undefined`, so `loadLocale` returns `Object.prototype` before the `isLocaleNameSane` check ever runs. `getSetGlobalLocale` then stores that value as the global locale with no `instanceof Locale` check, and every later formatting call throws because `Object.prototype` has none of the `Locale` methods. The global locale stays corrupted until it is set again explicitly. `constructor` and `prototype` reach the same code path.

### Minimal reproduction

```javascript
const moment = require('moment'); // 2.30.1

console.log(moment.locale());       // en
moment.locale('__proto__');
console.log(moment.locale());       // undefined
console.log(moment().format('LLLL')); // throws
```

### Actual behavior

```
en
undefined
TypeError: locale.longDateFormat is not a function
```

After `moment.locale('__proto__')`, `moment.locale()` returns `undefined` and every locale-dependent formatting call (`format` with locale tokens, `calendar()`, `fromNow()`) throws for the rest of the process, until `moment.locale('en')` (or another valid locale) is set again.

### Expected behavior

An unrecognized locale name, including `__proto__`, `constructor`, and `prototype`, should be treated as "not found" (warn and keep the current locale), exactly like any other unknown name. It should never replace the global locale with a non-`Locale` value.

### Moment.js version

2.30.1

### Runtime

Node.js 22.x and 24.x

### Loading method

npm CommonJS

### Locale

not applicable

### Time zone

not applicable

### Additional context

Root cause:
- `src/lib/locale/locales.js` declares `var locales = {}` (and `localeFamilies = {}`) as plain objects, so property lookups fall through to `Object.prototype`.
- `loadLocale()` uses `if (locales[name] !== undefined)` before `isLocaleNameSane`, so `__proto__` returns `Object.prototype` and short-circuits.
- `getSetGlobalLocale()` assigns any truthy `getLocale()` result to the global locale without an `instanceof Locale` check.

Possible fix directions: use `Object.create(null)` for the registries, replace `locales[name] !== undefined` with an explicit `hasOwnProp(locales, name)` check, run `isLocaleNameSane` (extended to reject `__proto__`/`constructor`/`prototype`) before any `locales[...]` access, and require `instanceof Locale` in `getSetGlobalLocale` before assigning the global locale.

Reported by @manqingzhou. Thanks for the analysis and reproduction.
items.title: [Bug] moment.locale('__proto__') corrupts the global locale and breaks formatting

items.body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I searched existing issues for this problem.
- [x] I read the applicable documentation and guides.
- [x] I reproduced the problem with the latest Moment.js release.
- [x] I confirmed this belongs to Moment.js core, not Moment Timezone, Luxon, or the momentjs.com website.

### Description

Moment.js does not validate that a timezone offset parsed from an ISO-8601 string, or passed numerically to `utcOffset()`, falls within the real world range of `-12:00` to `+14:00`. The hour and minute groups each accept any two digits (`00`-`99`), so the offset can reach 6039 minutes (about 4.19 days), and `isValid()` returns `true` for it, including in strict mode. Separately, `utcOffset(number)` infers hours vs minutes from the magnitude (`|input| < 16` is treated as hours), so two adjacent integers land far apart.

### Minimal reproduction

```javascript
const moment = require('moment'); // 2.30.1

// Out-of-range offset in an ISO string
const m = moment('2026-09-02T00:00:00+99:99');
console.log(m.isValid());     // true
console.log(m.toISOString()); // 2026-08-28T19:21:00.000Z

// Strict mode does not catch it either
console.log(moment('2026-09-02T00:00:00+99:99', moment.ISO_8601, true).isValid()); // true
console.log(moment.parseZone('2026-09-02T00:00:00+99:99').utcOffset());            // 6039

// Magnitude-based hours/minutes inference
console.log(moment().utcOffset(15).format('Z')); // +15:00
console.log(moment().utcOffset(16).format('Z')); // +00:16
```

### Actual behavior

```
true
2026-08-28T19:21:00.000Z
true
6039
+15:00
+00:16
```

`isValid()` is `true` for `+99:99`, and the parsed instant is silently shifted back about 4 days 4 hours 39 minutes. `utcOffset(15)` and `utcOffset(16)` differ by 14.7 hours.

### Expected behavior

An offset outside `-12:00`..`+14:00` should make `isValid()` return `false` (at least in strict mode), consistent with how other out-of-range fields are handled by `checkOverflow`. `utcOffset(15)` vs `utcOffset(16)` should not silently switch unit interpretation without a warning.

### Moment.js version

2.30.1

### Runtime

Node.js 24.16.0

### Loading method

npm CommonJS

### Locale

not applicable

### Time zone

not applicable (offset supplied in the input string)

### Additional context

Root cause:
- `src/lib/units/offset.js` `offsetFromString()` computes `minutes = parts[1] * 60 + parts[2]` with no bound on either group.
- The offset-matching regex (`matchShortOffset` / `matchOffset`) accepts `[+-]\d\d(?::?\d\d)?`.
- `src/lib/create/from-array.js` `checkOverflow()` validates Y/M/D/H/m/s/ms but never inspects `config._tzm`, so an out-of-range offset never flips `isValid()` to false, even in strict mode.
- `getSetOffset()` infers offset units from magnitude rather than an explicit flag.

Possible fix directions: range-check the offset in `offsetFromString()`, tighten the offset regex to the legal range (e.g. `[+-](?:0\d|1[0-4])(?::?[0-5]\d)?`), add `_tzm` to `checkOverflow()`, and consider deprecating the magnitude-based unit inference.

Reported by @manqingzhou. Thanks for the detailed analysis and reproduction.

I’ve looked at general GitHub documentation, but would like clarification as it pertains to moment/moment’s workflow.

If there are examples or guidelines previously discussed, linking those would be helpful.

items.body:
Hello maintainers,

First of all, thank you for maintaining Moment.js. It is a very helpful and widely used library.

While reading the documentation as a beginner, I found that most usage examples are clear, but I was a little confused about when to prefer Moment.js over newer alternatives mentioned in the docs.

I understand that Moment.js is now in maintenance mode, but it would be helpful for new users if there were a short summary explaining typical use cases where Moment.js is still recommended, especially for existing projects.

This is just a suggestion from a learner's perspective. Thank you for your great work!
items.title: Question about documentation clarity for new users
